title: Exact certification of a positive-order Rényi additivity violation for an explicit channel pair
abstract: Cubitt, Harrow, Leung, Montanaro, and Winter (CHLMW) exhibited an explicit pair of quantum channels whose minimum output Rényi entropy is nonadditive at order zero, and reported numerical violations at positive orders close to zero. Their paper states that a semidefinite-programming argument yields a rigorous positive-order interval for the same example, without printing the endpoint or a verifiable certificate; a recent paper by Leung, Lovitz, and Wu records that for this pair "no rigorous endpoint was obtained". We close that gap for the trace-preserving normalization of the printed pair fixed in Section 2. Small rational witness matrices prove that every output of either channel has all eigenvalues between $301/100000$ and $2/3$; a single explicit entangled input has an exact rational joint output spectrum of rank eight; and two independent elementary interval arguments turn these three facts into a proof of strict additivity violation, $S_p^{\min}(\mathrm{N}_R\otimes\mathrm{N}_{\bar S}) < S_p^{\min}(\mathrm{N}_R)+S_p^{\min}(\mathrm{N}_{\bar S}),$ for every real order $0<p\le 1/22$. Every step of the verification reduces to comparisons of integers, and the complete certificate is a few small rational matrices that a reader can check with a short program -- or, for any single order, by hand. To our knowledge, consistent with the assessment of Leung, Lovitz, and Wu, this is the first printed, computer-verifiable certified positive-order endpoint for this explicit pair. We claim no novelty for the phenomenon or for the eigenvalue-floor mechanism, both due to CHLMW, and no optimality of the endpoint.
summary: This paper rigorously proves a positive-order violation of Rényi additivity for a known pair of quantum channels. By developing two independent, computationally verifiable methods, the authors establish a certified interval ($0 < p \le 1/22$) for this violation. This work significantly advances the theoretical understanding of quantum channel properties by providing a concrete, checkable mathematical certificate.
main_problem: To provide the first printed, computer-verifiable certified positive-order endpoint for the violation of Rényi additivity for a specific pair of quantum channels.
main_result: The authors prove a strict violation of Rényi additivity, $S_p^{\min}(N_R\otimes N_{ ar S}) < S_p^{\min}(N_R)+S_p^{\min}(N_{ ar S})$, for the interval $0 < p \le 1/22$.
method: The proof uses elementary, certificate-based methods, including staircase arguments and derivative analysis, relying on comparisons of integers to establish the required inequality.
model_or_system: The study concerns two explicit quantum channels, $N_R$ and $ ar{N}_S$, acting on specific subspaces derived from the CHLMW example.
key_observables: Minimum output Rényi entropy, $S_{\min}^p(N) = \min_{ho} S_p(N(ho))$, and the additivity inequality.
important_parameters: The violation is certified for the order $0 < p \le 1/22$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on establishing the inequality $A(p)^2 > B(p)$ for the specified interval, and the endpoint $1/22$ is not claimed to be optimal.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by referencing previous work, then uses eigenvalue bounds and concavity arguments to set up the core inequality, which is finally proven using two independent, rigorous methods (staircase and derivative) to certify the interval $(0, 1/22]$.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly rigorous, computationally verifiable certificate for a fundamental quantum information phenomenon (Rényi additivity violation), which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum channel capacity.
